claim: This type is eight peaking sections parked at fixed centres, one output pan and one level, with a single width byte driving all eight instead of one each. The centres are the named third octaves at 250, 500, 1k, 1.25k, 2k, 3.15k, 4k and 8k: a band raised to the top of its byte and cut to the bottom returns the same centre to within 0.02 octaves, and the eight sit 0.030 octaves under the named series with a scatter of 0.018 -- which is the offset this unit's other equaliser's table was measured to carry. That offset has since been measured to be the unit's rather than the reading's, by putting a section of known centre through the same band set, window and fit at the width both types were read at, where it comes back on the name to two thousandths of an octave -- so the eight really do sit below the series they are named by. With each type's own mean taken out the seven centres the two types share still run the same way, over a pattern 0.046 octaves wide that they disagree about by 0.012 at worst and 0.006 in the median. Whether that is one table or two tables computed the same way is not separated here. The width byte indexes five entries and four of them are the equaliser's Q byte's entries exactly: 2.583, 1.417, 0.750 and 0.417 octaves between the half-gain points, on a reading whose step is a twelfth. Past the fifth printed step the two types disagree. This one returns the fifth entry and the equaliser returns the first, so what is shared is the table and not the handling of a byte outside it. Each band gain answers over the twenty-five values from 52 to 76 and returns the nearest end for everything outside, and the power-on state is the eight defaults its own page prints, read through a width byte the page prints no default for and which powers up at its third entry.
named: The eight band gains at 40 03 03 through 40 03 0A, the width byte at 40 03 0B and the pan at 40 03 15, on type 01 01.
adds: Three standing claims reach this type for the first time and one of them is cut back. The gain class claim and the width claim did not name 01 01 at all; the pan class claim named it and had never been held against a record on it. What is new beyond that reach is the structure: eight sections at fixed centres is not a shorter equaliser, it is the same sections with the frequency byte removed and replaced by a position in the table, and one width byte serving all eight rather than one per section is the arrangement that makes eight sections cost what four did. The cut is to the width claim, whose rule for a byte past the printed steps holds on the type it was fitted on and not on this one.

document_rows.why: The eleven parameters this type prints and the range against each. Eight of them carry a middle figure, which is where the power-on gains are predicted from; the width byte's range is a list of five with no middle, which is why its own default is measured here rather than read off. Evidence about what a page states and not about the unit.

era_priors.claim: A graphic equaliser of this period shares one width across its sections rather than giving each its own.
era_priors.why: A section's coefficients are recomputed when its width moves. One shared width is one recomputation for eight sections and one byte of state; eight widths are eight of each, which is what makes eight sections cost more than twice what four do.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The page printed a width per band, or the one it prints moved some bands and not others. It prints one, and the one it prints returns the same five entries this unit's parametric equaliser returns from its own per-section width byte -- so the sharing is in how many bytes there are, not in a cheaper filter.

alternatives.reading: The eight centres are the named third octaves themselves, and the 0.030 octaves both this type and the equaliser's table sit under them is carried by the reading rather than by the unit.
alternatives.why_it_matters: Only for what the agreement is evidence of. The eight centres are where they are either way, and so is everything the width byte does.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The reading was measured to return a known centre at the width both types were read at: a mean of +0.0001 octaves over the eight with a scatter of 0.0019, against a term of 0.030. Nothing is left for the reading to carry.

alternatives.reading: The width byte is not written above its fifth printed step, so what the high settings return is whatever the type was already holding.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The type powers up with that byte at its third entry, which this run measured rather than assumed -- the takes with nothing written return the third step's profile to a tenth of a decibel across twenty-two bands. A refused write would therefore leave 1.417 octaves between the half-gain points. Bytes five, sixty-four and a hundred and twenty-seven all return 0.417, which is the fifth entry. The write is taken and held at the top of the table.

alternatives.reading: The eighth band is past the end of the table, rather than past what four bits of a frequency byte can reach of it.

separated_by.observable: Where a table entry above 6.3k sits, asked through a byte that indexes the table rather than through a section parked at one of its entries.

predicts.the table ends at the sixteenth entry: nothing indexes an entry above 6166.8, and the eighth band is a section placed outside the table
predicts.the table is longer than four bits reach: an entry near 7900 exists and something indexes it

separated_by.sensitivity_here: Not a question of resolution. The eighth band sits 0.36 octaves above the highest entry the equaliser's byte returns, which is twenty times the scatter of the eight and far outside any reading's own spread. What is missing is a byte to ask with.
separated_by.why_not_separable: No byte in the printed tables indexes a peaking centre above 6.3k. The equaliser's own high corner prints 4k and 8k, but it is a two-state shelf and what it moves is where a slope runs steepest -- 9.5k against 11.3k between its two states, with the profile still rising at the top of the band set in both. That says where a shelf hinges and not where a table entry sits, so it cannot be held against a centre. Until a type is found whose frequency byte reaches past 6.3k, a seventeenth entry and a section outside the table predict the same eight numbers, and this is a margin of one -- the bar this project refuses to queue below.

refuted_by: A band whose raised and cut takes disagree about its centre by more than the spread the other seven show, which would mean the eight are not fixed sections but something whose position moves with its gain. A width setting whose half-gain span differs from the equaliser's at the four entries the band set contains by more than the twelfth of an octave the reading steps in. A gain byte answering outside 52 to 76.
what_it_would_change: Two class claims gain a type and one is cut back. A renderer for this type is eight of the sections the equaliser claim already describes, at seven of the entries the frequency claim already lists and one above them, behind one shared width -- so nothing new has to be modelled for it beyond the fixed positions. And the width claim's rule for a byte past its printed steps becomes a property of the type rather than of the byte, which is the kind of thing a renderer gets wrong silently because no setting a musician uses reaches it.
what_this_does_not_settle: Whether the centres are entries of one shared table or two uses of one named series, which is the standing alternative and costs nothing to settle. What the level byte does, which was not asked. Whether the eight sections are in a chain or summed in parallel: a band profile is magnitude and eight sections at 0 dB are unity either way, which is also why the flat reference this run measured against is the same reference under both. The pan byte's table, which five settings cannot count -- what they say is that its centre sits 2.67 dB under its end, neither the 3.01 of a constant-power pair nor the 6.02 of a crossfade, and that is one figure of a table the pan claim reads nineteen entries in.
what_it_was_predicted_from: The prediction was written before the unit was booked and names what each of the four claims reaching this type would have to return. Two parts of it were wrong and the record of that is worth more than the parts that landed. The width claim's rule for settings past the printed steps was predicted to hold and it does not. And the page's eight printed defaults were predicted to be what the type powers up holding, which they are -- but the prediction could not say what depth they would be read at, because the width byte they are read through is printed as a list with no middle and so has no printed default. That gap was written down before the run and is why the power-on gains were taken again through each of the five widths, which is what put the byte's own default at the third entry.

where_the_eight_sit_hz.why_those_two_lines_are_the_whole_point: They are the same number. A comparison that quotes how much better these eight agree with the equaliser's measured entries than with the named series is quoting a term that sits on both sides of it.
where_the_eight_sit_hz.and_whose_term_it_is: Measured, and it is the unit's. A section of known centre put through this band set, window and fit at the width both types were read at comes back on the name: +0.0001 octaves over the eight with a scatter of 0.0019. The sentence above still holds -- the term does sit on both sides of that comparison and the ratio is still not quotable -- but the eight really are below the series, and what survives taking each type's mean out is under 0.012 octaves band by band.

half_gain_span_in_octaves.why_byte_nought_is_not_held_against_the_: The widest entry runs past the ends of the band set, so where its half-gain points fall is set by where the reading stops rather than by the section. The two types differ there by three twelfths and agree exactly at the four entries the band set contains.

the_gain_ladder_on_one_band_db.why_it_is_not_a_decibel_a_step_here: Twelve steps return 11.57 and not 12.00, and four and eight steps return 3.79 and 7.56. A band reading averages over a band, and the peak it is averaging is 0.417 octaves wide against bands a twelfth of an octave apart, so a tall narrow feature is reported shorter than it is. Read at a third of an octave the same takes return 9.7 instead of 11.57, which is the dilution doubling as the band widens. The window and the sticking are read exactly; the step size is not what this reading returns.

what_the_width_byte_powers_up_at.how_it_was_read: The two takes with nothing written to any of the eleven bytes return the profile the third printed step returns, band for band, to a tenth of a decibel over twenty-two bands. The page prints this byte as a list of five figures with no middle, so it names no default for it and the value is measured rather than read off.

the_round_that_rendered_a_centre_it_alre.what_was_asked: Whether the 0.030 octaves these eight centres and the equaliser's sixteen entries both sit under the third octaves the page names them by is a property of the unit or of the way this archive reads where a peak is. No record could answer it: every figure on both sides went through one fit, so the term is on both sides of every comparison that could be made between them.
the_round_that_rendered_a_centre_it_alre.how_it_was_run: The audio cookbook's peaking section, at a centre chosen rather than fitted, rendered onto the same flat takes this run measured its own reference from and read out through the same band energies, the same half-gain window and the same parabola. Eight centres, both signs of the gain, and each of the five widths the printed table holds, at both band sets. The width matters and is not a free choice: both the eight sections and the equaliser's sixteen entries were read with that byte at its fifth entry, which the equaliser's record names in its own held block.
the_round_that_rendered_a_centre_it_alre.what_came_back: At that width the reading returns the centre it was given. Over the eight named positions the mean is +0.0001 octaves with a scatter of 0.0019, and four of the eight land below rather than eight of eight. That is a thirtieth of the term being explained and it does not lean. The term is the unit's.
the_round_that_rendered_a_centre_it_alre.why_three_estimators_and_not_one: Because the rendered section is the audio cookbook's peaking biquad and the unit's need not be, and every reading of a centre assumes something about the shape it is reading. So the eight were read three ways, by estimators that assume less each time. The parabola is the published one, fitted over the feature's own half-gain window. The second renders the section at a ladder of centres about each name and matches it against the unit's whole measured profile over every band that cleared the run's floor, one level factor fitted out -- no parabola, but still that section's shape. The third walks out from the largest band to where the deviation falls to half on each side, interpolates both crossings and takes their geometric mean: it assumes only that the feature is symmetric about its centre in log frequency, which is the weakest thing that can be assumed by anything calling a number a centre. The three return -0.0297, -0.0306 and -0.0331 octaves, eight of eight below on all three. The third was put through the rendered known centre too, where it returns between -0.0056 and +0.0037.
the_round_that_rendered_a_centre_it_alre.what_the_whole_shape_match_cost_says: Less than it looks, and the figure is published rather than described. Moving the rendered section from where it matches best to the name it is called by costs between 0.03 and 0.32 dB of the match's own residual, against a residual of 0.36 to 0.60 dB. So no single band's profile chooses strongly between the two, and what carries this estimator is that all eight choose the same way. The residual itself is the more useful number: 0.36 to 0.60 dB against features twelve decibels tall is the floor the run's own flat repeats drew, so the unit's sections are this shape to within what the takes can say.
the_round_that_rendered_a_centre_it_alre.what_is_left_of_the_shape_question: A section that is not symmetric in log frequency. All three estimators return a centre, and a feature with a longer flank on one side has no single centre for them to agree on -- the third would need the two half-gain arms to differ by 0.066 octaves against a span of 0.417, with the lower arm the shorter. Nothing here rules that out by itself. What bounds it is the whole-profile residual: a symmetric section of the cookbook's form already accounts for the measured profile down to the run's floor, so the asymmetry left over to hide in is the floor's size. This is written as what the run did not close rather than as a fourth reading, because it is not a different table -- it is the same entries read through a section whose shape would make where the centre is a different question from the one the page's names answer.
the_round_that_rendered_a_centre_it_alre.the_one_term_this_cannot_cancel: A sample rate that is wrong. Rendering onto a take and then reading that take puts the same assumed rate on both sides, so a rate that is off by a factor moves the model and the unit together and comes back as no bias at all -- which is exactly the shape of what is being explained. It is asked of a take whose frequency is known from outside the reading: the held tone the type survey was taken on, recorded as 440 Hz in that stage's own invocation, reads 439.966. That is -0.00011 octaves, two hundred and seventy times smaller than the term.
the_round_that_rendered_a_centre_it_alre.what_the_reading_does_carry: A bias that grows with the width of the feature and with where it sits, and at the broad end it is large. The same rendering read at the first of the five printed widths returns a centre 0.26 octaves low at 8k and 0.02 low at 250, and at the third width 0.04 low at 8k. This is the bias the band record's own `why_fitted` describes and it is now measured rather than described: it is under a hundredth of an octave everywhere at the two narrowest widths, and it is not something a reader may carry across to a figure read at a broad one. The claims here are unaffected because both types' centres were read at the narrowest.
the_round_that_rendered_a_centre_it_alre.what_it_does_not_close: Whether the eight centres and the equaliser's entries are one table or two tables computed the same way. What the term being the unit's changes is which comparison is admissible: the ratio of how well these eight agree with the equaliser's measured entries against how well they agree with the named series is still not quotable, because a term shared by two things inflates their agreement whatever put it there. What is quotable is the part that survives taking each type's own mean out, and that is now evidence where before it was unreadable. It does not choose between one table and two tables written from one derivation, which no reading of an output can.

what_survives_taking_each_types_mean_out.what_that_is_against: The size of the pattern itself and the spread of this reading's own repeats. About their means the seven run over 0.046 octaves, so a disagreement of 0.012 at worst is a quarter of what is being agreed about; and the claim records one band's two takes as disagreeing by 0.0005 to 0.0286 octaves, so the disagreement between the types sits inside what one type's own repeats show. It does not choose between one table and two tables written from one derivation, which predict the same pattern.
